title: The Lord Is Come, the Heavens Proclaim
description: The Lord Is Come, the Heavens Proclaim in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 97, part 2, headed “Christ's incarnation”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord is come, the heavens pro-claim His birth; the na-tions learn his Name; An un-known star di-rects the road Of east-ern sa-ges to their God.

lines: The Lord is come, the heavens proclaim
His birth; the nations learn his Name;
An unknown star directs the road
Of eastern sages to their God.
All ye bright armies of the skies,
Go, worship where the Saviour lies:
Angels and kings before him bow,
Those gods on high, and gods below.
Let idols totter to the ground,
But Judah shout, but Zion sing,
And earth confess her sovereign King.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
